summary: Suspected vishing-led credential disclosure; service-account key used from unfamiliar IPs
description: Issue summary: Security team received alert that a long-lived service-account key (svc-data-ingest-prod) was used to access internal ingestion endpoints following a suspected vishing call to an engineer. Impact: potential unauthorized access to telemetry payloads and export of usage metadata. Initial detection: anomalous key usage flagged by audit-logging rules and a subsequent employee report.
impact: Potentially exfiltrated telemetry/metrics data associated with production ingestion pipelines; no customer PII identified so far. Access window estimated ~2026-03-11T23:30Z to 2026-03-12T01:10Z.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Security rules detect key usage from new public IPs. 2) Automated log alert triggers on unusual downstream export. 3) On-call reaches out to employee who reports a suspicious phone call requesting 'service key' confirmation. 4) Rotate compromised key and validate downstream consumers.
logs:
Audit log excerpts:
- 2026-03-11T23:37:12Z svc-data-ingest-prod key auth from 3.128.45.99 (ASN: AS16509).
- 2026-03-11T23:41:55Z ingest.upload.start: req_id=rr-9a3b, dataset=telemetry-metrics, bytes=1.2MB.
- 2026-03-12T00:55:02Z svc-data-ingest-prod key auth from 18.205.33.18 (ASN: AS14618).
- Full log export saved to s3://redwood-security/forensic/INT-252712/logs-2026-03-12.log
investigation_notes: Employee (eng) received a phone call claiming to be finance requesting 'access confirmation' for a legacy ingestion key; employee relayed partial key fingerprint over phone before call ended.
No signs of lateral movement within our VPCs; observed API activity limited to ingestion endpoints and S3 put operations in telemetry bucket during access window.
IP addresses map to cloud provider ranges (AWS); historical patterns show those ASNs previously used by legitimate partners but no prior use of this key from these exact IPs.
Audit trail shows key last rotated 2025-10-02; key permissions include write to telemetry buckets and read-list on internal indexing service.
Forensic snapshot requested from S3 and object-level logs enabled; packet-level captures not available for the time window.
Triage suggests credential disclosure via social engineering (vishing) as highest-likelihood hypothesis.
actions_taken: 2026-03-12 01:25Z: Rotated svc-data-ingest-prod key; revoked old key via IAM console and enforced immediate expiration.
2026-03-12 01:40Z: Blocklisted originating IPs at edge WAF rules and created temporary firewall rule to block the two observed public IPs.
2026-03-12 02:15Z: Scoped down permissions on new key to write-only for designated ingestion prefixes; removed list/read permissions on indexing service pending review.
2026-03-12 03:00Z: Notified Data Governance and Customer Privacy teams; created retention hold on affected telemetry objects for forensic review.
2026-03-12 04:00Z: Initiated mandatory internal phishing/vishing awareness blast to engineering org and scheduled immediate all-hands security brief.
2026-03-12 05:30Z: Created follow-up ticket for onboarding MFA/phone verification changes to access-key disclosure policy (INT-252819).
2026-03-12 06:00Z: Eng SRE ran integrity checks on downstream consumers; no evidence of unexplained config changes or code commits tied to the event.
resolution: Mitigation in place: compromised key revoked, permissions tightened on replacement key, affected objects preserved for forensics, and awareness communications sent. Pending actions: complete forensic review, decide on external disclosure if exposure expands, and update access policies to prevent voice-based key disclosure.
